{"questions": [
{
"id": "p1",
"topic": "lattice points on a circle (sums of two squares)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "A circle centered at the origin passes through the point (50, 55). How many lattice points lie on this circle?",
"answer": 48,
"target_wrong": 40,
"error_description": "The representation 5525 = 41^2 + 62^2 is left out of the list of ways to write 5525 as a sum of two squares, losing the 8 points (+-41, +-62), (+-62, +-41).",
"cases": ["7^2+74^2 -> 8 points", "14^2+73^2 -> 8 points", "22^2+71^2 -> 8 points", "25^2+70^2 -> 8 points", "41^2+62^2 -> 8 points", "50^2+55^2 -> 8 points"],
"solution": "The radius squared is 50^2 + 55^2 = 2500 + 3025 = 5525 = 5^2 * 13 * 17. We need all integer solutions of x^2 + y^2 = 5525. Checking 5525 - x^2 for squares with 0 <= x <= y gives exactly the representations 5525 = 7^2 + 74^2 = 14^2 + 73^2 = 22^2 + 71^2 = 25^2 + 70^2 = 41^2 + 62^2 = 50^2 + 55^2. (Check: 49+5476, 196+5329, 484+5041, 625+4900, 1681+3844, 2500+3025 all equal 5525.) In every representation the two parts are distinct and nonzero, so each contributes 2*2*2 = 8 lattice points (two orders, two signs each). Hence there are 6 * 8 = 48 lattice points. As a check, the number of representations is 4(d_1 - d_3) where d_i counts divisors congruent to i mod 4; all 12 divisors of 5525 are 1 mod 4, so 4 * 12 = 48.",
"check_code": "import math\nr2=50*50+55*55\nm=math.isqrt(r2)\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(-m,m+1):\n    for y in range(-m,m+1):\n        if x*x+y*y==r2:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "circles x^2+y^2=n through exactly 8 lattice points",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers n with n <= 50 for which the circle x^2 + y^2 = n passes through exactly 8 lattice points.",
"answer": 317,
"target_wrong": 272,
"error_description": "n = 45 = 3^2 + 6^2 (= 9 * 5) is omitted; solvers listing 5, 10, 20, 40 and the primes 13, 17, 29, 37, 41 with their doubles 26, 34 tend to forget that multiplying by the square 9 keeps exactly 8 points.",
"cases": ["n=5", "n=10", "n=13", "n=17", "n=20", "n=26", "n=29", "n=34", "n=37", "n=40", "n=41", "n=45"],
"solution": "Write n = 2^a * m * k^2 where m is a product of primes congruent to 1 mod 4 and k is a product of primes congruent to 3 mod 4 (n has no lattice points at all unless the 3-mod-4 primes appear to even powers). The number of lattice points on x^2 + y^2 = n is 4 * tau(m), where tau(m) is the number of divisors of m. Exactly 8 points means tau(m) = 2, i.e. m is a single prime p congruent to 1 mod 4 appearing to the first power. For n <= 50: p = 5 gives n = 5, 10, 20, 40 (times powers of 2) and 45 (times 9); p = 13 gives 13, 26; p = 17 gives 17, 34; p = 29, 37, 41 give themselves. (25 and 50 have 12 points since m = 25, and 52 = 4*13 exceeds 50.) Direct check, e.g. 45 = 3^2 + 6^2 gives (+-3,+-6),(+-6,+-3): 8 points. The sum is 5 + 10 + 13 + 17 + 20 + 26 + 29 + 34 + 37 + 40 + 41 + 45 = 317.",
"check_code": "import math\ntot=0\nfor n in range(1,51):\n    m=math.isqrt(n)\n    c=0\n    for x in range(-m,m+1):\n        for y in range(-m,m+1):\n            if x*x+y*y==n:\n                c+=1\n    if c==8:\n        tot+=n\nprint(tot)"
},
{
"id": "p3",
"topic": "right angles subtended by a segment (Thales circle) at lattice points",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Let A = (0, 0) and B = (65, 0). How many lattice points P are there such that angle APB is a right angle?",
"answer": 16,
"target_wrong": 12,
"error_description": "The representation 65^2 = 33^2 + 56^2 (the 33-56-65 triple) is omitted from the list 16^2+63^2, 25^2+60^2, 39^2+52^2, losing the four points (16,+-28) and (49,+-28).",
"cases": ["65^2 = 16^2+63^2 -> (1,+-8),(64,+-8)", "65^2 = 25^2+60^2 -> (20,+-30),(45,+-30)", "65^2 = 33^2+56^2 -> (16,+-28),(49,+-28)", "65^2 = 39^2+52^2 -> (13,+-26),(52,+-26)"],
"solution": "Angle APB = 90 degrees exactly when P lies on the circle with diameter AB, other than A and B themselves. That circle is (x - 65/2)^2 + y^2 = (65/2)^2, i.e. (2x - 65)^2 + (2y)^2 = 65^2. Set u = 2x - 65 (odd) and v = 2y (even); we need u^2 + v^2 = 4225 with u odd, v even. Since 65^2 = 5^2 * 13^2 has 9 divisors, all 1 mod 4, there are 36 integer solutions of u^2 + v^2 = 4225, coming from 4225 = 0^2 + 65^2 = 16^2 + 63^2 = 25^2 + 60^2 = 33^2 + 56^2 = 39^2 + 52^2. The representation 0^2 + 65^2 forces (u, v) = (+-65, 0), i.e. P = A or P = B, which give no angle. Each of the other four representations has one odd and one even part, giving u = +-(odd part), v = +-(even part): 4 solutions each, hence 4 lattice points each: (1,+-8),(64,+-8); (20,+-30),(45,+-30); (16,+-28),(49,+-28); (13,+-26),(52,+-26). Total 4 * 4 = 16 lattice points.",
"check_code": "cnt=0\nfor x in range(-100,200):\n    for y in range(-100,101):\n        if (x,y)==(0,0) or (x,y)==(65,0):\n            continue\n        if x*(x-65)+y*y==0:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p4",
"topic": "lattice points on a line at integer distance from the origin (factor pairs)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many lattice points on the line y = 24 are at an integer distance from the origin?",
"answer": 15,
"target_wrong": 14,
"error_description": "The factor pair 24 * 24 of 576 (giving x = 0, the point (0, 24) at distance 24) is omitted; only the pairs with distinct factors, which give x = +-7, +-10, +-18, +-32, +-45, +-70, +-143, are counted.",
"cases": ["(2,288) -> x=+-143", "(4,144) -> x=+-70", "(6,96) -> x=+-45", "(8,72) -> x=+-32", "(12,48) -> x=+-18", "(16,36) -> x=+-10", "(18,32) -> x=+-7", "(24,24) -> x=0"],
"solution": "A point (x, 24) is at distance d from the origin where x^2 + 576 = d^2, so (d - x)(d + x) = 576 with d >= 0. Since d - x and d + x have the same parity and 576 is even, both are even; writing d - x = 2e, d + x = 2f gives ef = 144 with e <= f (taking x >= 0). The factor pairs of 144 are (1,144), (2,72), (3,48), (4,36), (6,24), (8,18), (9,16), (12,12), giving x = f - e = 143, 70, 45, 32, 18, 10, 7, 0 and d = 145, 74, 51, 40, 30, 26, 25, 24. Each nonzero x gives two points (x and -x), and x = 0 gives one. Total: 7 * 2 + 1 = 15 lattice points.",
"check_code": "import math\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(-2000,2001):\n    d=x*x+576\n    s=math.isqrt(d)\n    if s*s==d:\n        cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p5",
"topic": "integer-length chords between lattice points on a circle",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many chords of the circle x^2 + y^2 = 50 have both endpoints at lattice points and have integer length?",
"answer": 20,
"target_wrong": 16,
"error_description": "The lattice points (+-5, +-5) (from 50 = 5^2 + 5^2) are omitted when listing the points on the circle; only the eight points from 50 = 1^2 + 7^2 are used, losing the 4 chords of length 10 among the (+-5, +-5) points.",
"cases": ["chords among (+-1,+-7): (1,7)-(1,-7) type length 14 (2 chords), (1,7)-(-1,7) type length 2 (2 chords)", "chords among (+-7,+-1): length 14 (2 chords), length 2 (2 chords)", "chords among (+-5,+-5): length 10 (4 chords)", "chords between (+-1,+-7) and (+-7,+-1): length 10 (8 chords)"],
"solution": "The lattice points on x^2 + y^2 = 50 come from 50 = 1^2 + 7^2 = 5^2 + 5^2: the 8 points (+-1,+-7), (+-7,+-1) and the 4 points (+-5,+-5), 12 points in all. Group them as A = {(+-1,+-7)}, B = {(+-7,+-1)}, C = {(+-5,+-5)}. Within A: (1,7)-(1,-7) has length 14 and (1,7)-(-1,7) has length 2 (integers), while (1,7)-(-1,-7) has length sqrt(200); so A gives 2 + 2 = 4 integer chords, and by symmetry B gives 4. Within C: (5,5)-(5,-5) and (5,5)-(-5,5) have length 10, and (5,5)-(-5,-5) has length sqrt(200); C gives 4 chords. Between A and B: from (1,7), the distances to (7,1), (7,-1), (-7,1), (-7,-1) are sqrt(72), 10, 10, sqrt(128); so each of the 4 points of A has 2 integer chords to B, giving 8. Between A (or B) and C: from (1,7) the squared distances to (5,5), (5,-5), (-5,5), (-5,-5) are 20, 160, 40, 180, none a square, and similarly for B; no chords. Total 4 + 4 + 4 + 8 = 20.",
"check_code": "import math\npts=[(x,y) for x in range(-8,9) for y in range(-8,9) if x*x+y*y==50]\ncnt=0\nfor i in range(len(pts)):\n    for j in range(i+1,len(pts)):\n        d=(pts[i][0]-pts[j][0])**2+(pts[i][1]-pts[j][1])**2\n        s=math.isqrt(d)\n        if s*s==d:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p6",
"topic": "lattice points at integer distance from the origin (Pythagorean legs)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many lattice points (x, y) with 1 <= x <= 25 and 1 <= y <= 25 are at an integer distance from the origin?",
"answer": 22,
"target_wrong": 20,
"error_description": "The primitive triple (20, 21, 29) is omitted from the list of Pythagorean triples with both legs at most 25, losing the two points (20, 21) and (21, 20).",
"cases": ["(3,4)", "(6,8)", "(9,12)", "(12,16)", "(15,20)", "(18,24)", "(5,12)", "(10,24)", "(8,15)", "(7,24)", "(20,21)"],
"solution": "We need x^2 + y^2 to be a perfect square with 1 <= x, y <= 25, i.e. (x, y) is a pair of legs of a Pythagorean triple with both legs at most 25. The hypotenuse is at most sqrt(2)*25 < 36. Primitive triples with hypotenuse below 36 are (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25), (20,21,29); (12,35,37) and beyond have a leg exceeding 25. Multiples with both legs <= 25: from (3,4): k = 1,...,6 giving (3,4),(6,8),(9,12),(12,16),(15,20),(18,24); from (5,12): (5,12),(10,24); from (8,15): (8,15) only (16,30 fails); from (7,24): (7,24); from (20,21): (20,21). That is 11 unordered leg pairs, each with distinct legs, so each gives two ordered lattice points (x,y) and (y,x). Total 22.",
"check_code": "import math\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(1,26):\n    for y in range(1,26):\n        d=x*x+y*y\n        s=math.isqrt(d)\n        if s*s==d:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p7",
"topic": "tangent circles with lattice centers",
"error_type": "misapplied_formula",
"question": "How many lattice points (a, b) are there for which the circle with center (a, b) and radius 12 is tangent to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 169?",
"answer": 24,
"target_wrong": 20,
"error_description": "The tangency condition d = r_1 + r_2 is applied as if it were the only one, ignoring internal tangency d = |r_1 - r_2| = 1; this counts only the 20 solutions of a^2 + b^2 = 625 and misses the 4 solutions of a^2 + b^2 = 1.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Two circles of radii 13 and 12 are tangent exactly when the distance d between their centers is 13 + 12 = 25 (external tangency) or 13 - 12 = 1 (internal tangency, the radius-12 circle inside the radius-13 circle). So we need a^2 + b^2 = 625 or a^2 + b^2 = 1. For 625 = 5^4: 625 = 0^2 + 25^2 = 7^2 + 24^2 = 15^2 + 20^2, giving (0,+-25),(+-25,0) [4 points] plus (+-7,+-24),(+-24,+-7),(+-15,+-20),(+-20,+-15) [16 points], i.e. 20 lattice points (consistent with 4*tau(625) = 20). For a^2 + b^2 = 1 there are 4 lattice points (+-1,0),(0,+-1). Total 20 + 4 = 24.",
"check_code": "cnt=0\nR,r=13,12\nfor a in range(-30,31):\n    for b in range(-30,31):\n        d2=a*a+b*b\n        if d2==(R+r)**2 or d2==(R-r)**2:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p8",
"topic": "difference of distances to two points (squaring an equation)",
"error_type": "algebra_slip",
"question": "Let A = (0, 12) and B = (21, 0). Find the sum of all real numbers x such that the point P = (x, 0) is exactly 3 units farther from A than from B.",
"answer": 9,
"target_wrong": 14,
"error_description": "Squaring sqrt(x^2+144) = |x-21| + 3 twice yields x^2 - 14x + 45 = 0, and both roots x = 5 and x = 9 are accepted without checking; x = 5 is extraneous (there PB - PA = 3, not PA - PB = 3), so the slipped sum is 5 + 9 = 14.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "We need PA = PB + 3, i.e. sqrt(x^2 + 144) = |x - 21| + 3. Case x >= 21: sqrt(x^2 + 144) = x - 18, so x^2 + 144 = x^2 - 36x + 324, giving x = 5, which contradicts x >= 21; no solution. Case x < 21: sqrt(x^2 + 144) = 24 - x, so x^2 + 144 = 576 - 48x + x^2, giving x = 9, and indeed 24 - 9 > 0, PA = sqrt(81 + 144) = 15, PB = 12, PA - PB = 3. (The value x = 5 satisfies the squared equation because at (5,0) we have PA = 13 and PB = 16, so PB - PA = 3, the opposite branch of the hyperbola.) The only solution is x = 9, so the requested sum is 9.",
"check_code": "from fractions import Fraction as F\na,b,c=12,21,3\nroots=set()\nfor s in (1,-1):\n    den=2*(s*c-b)\n    if den==0:\n        continue\n    x=F(a*a-b*b-c*c+2*s*c*b,den)\n    t=s*(x-b)\n    if t>=0 and x*x+a*a==(t+c)**2:\n        roots.add(x)\nprint(int(sum(roots)))"
},
{
"id": "p9",
"topic": "lattice points in exactly one of two disks",
"error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "How many lattice points are at distance at most 5 from exactly one of the two points A = (0, 0) and B = (7, 0)?",
"answer": 130,
"target_wrong": 146,
"error_description": "\"Exactly one\" is read as \"at least one\": the union of the two disks is counted, 81 + 81 - 16 = 146, instead of the symmetric difference 81 + 81 - 2*16 = 130.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Count lattice points in a closed disk of radius 5: for y = 0, |x| <= 5 (11 points); y = +-1, +-2, +-3: x^2 <= 24, 21, 16 give |x| <= 4 (9 points each, 54 total); y = +-4: x^2 <= 9, 7 points each (14); y = +-5: 1 point each (2). Total 81. Each disk has 81 lattice points. Points in both disks satisfy x^2 + y^2 <= 25 and (x-7)^2 + y^2 <= 25, forcing 2 <= x <= 5: x = 2 gives y^2 <= 0 (1 point), x = 3 gives y^2 <= min(16, 9) = 9 (7 points), x = 4 gives y^2 <= min(9, 16) = 9 (7 points), x = 5 gives y^2 <= 0 (1 point); 16 points in the intersection. Points in exactly one disk: (81 - 16) + (81 - 16) = 130.",
"check_code": "cnt=0\nfor x in range(-10,20):\n    for y in range(-10,11):\n        a=x*x+y*y<=25\n        b=(x-7)**2+y*y<=25\n        if a!=b:\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
},
{
"id": "p10",
"topic": "interior lattice points of a lattice parallelogram (Pick's theorem)",
"error_type": "double_counting",
"question": "How many lattice points lie strictly inside the parallelogram with vertices (0, 0), (20, 8), (14, 26), and (-6, 18)?",
"answer": 399,
"target_wrong": 397,
"error_description": "The boundary count is taken as the sum of gcd + 1 over the four sides, 5 + 7 + 5 + 7 = 24, so each vertex is counted twice (true boundary count is 20); Pick's theorem then gives 408 - 12 + 1 = 397 instead of 408 - 10 + 1 = 399.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "The side vectors are u = (20, 8) and v = (-6, 18), so the area is |20*18 - 8*(-6)| = 360 + 48 = 408. The number of lattice points on the segment from one lattice point to another with displacement (p, q) is gcd(|p|, |q|) + 1 including both endpoints, so going around the boundary each side contributes exactly gcd(|p|, |q|) new points (counting each vertex once): gcd(20,8) + gcd(6,18) + gcd(20,8) + gcd(6,18) = 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 = 20 boundary lattice points. By Pick's theorem, Area = I + B/2 - 1, so I = 408 - 20/2 + 1 = 399.",
"check_code": "V=[(0,0),(20,8),(14,26),(-6,18)]\ndef inside(px,py):\n    sg=0\n    for i in range(4):\n        x1,y1=V[i]\n        x2,y2=V[(i+1)%4]\n        cr=(x2-x1)*(py-y1)-(y2-y1)*(px-x1)\n        if cr==0:\n            return False\n        if sg==0:\n            sg=1 if cr>0 else -1\n        elif (cr>0)!=(sg>0):\n            return False\n    return True\ncnt=0\nfor x in range(-10,25):\n    for y in range(-5,30):\n        if inside(x,y):\n            cnt+=1\nprint(cnt)"
}
]}
